title: Resolving the stellar activity of the Mira AB binary with ALMA
question: What are the size, shape, flux densities and spectral indices of Mira A and Mira B at mm wavelengths, and what do they imply about the extended atmosphere, stellar activity and the wind around Mira B?

data.angular_resolution: Band 3: 72x64 mas and 68x57 mas; Band 6: 34x24 mas

what.value: Flux density at 345 GHz and CO/continuum Cycle 1 ALMA data of Mira

evidence.quote: the flux density at 345 GHz (cite: ramsetal14) are presented in Fig. [3](#fig:sed)

what.value: VLA flux densities and 43 GHz measurements used in SED

evidence.quote: The VLA values, the ALMA values from this work and the flux density at 345 GHz (cite: ramsetal14) are presented in Fig. [3](#fig:sed).

what.value: Calibrator flux densities and spectral indices from the ALMA calibrator catalog

evidence.quote: we present the calibrators, and their adopted flux densities and spectral indices from the ALMA calibrator catalog.

recipe.method: Self-calibration on averaged continuum SPWs; images made with clean, Briggs 0.5, MFS with 2 Taylor terms in Band 3

recipe.goal: Fit source size and shape in uv-plane
recipe.method: uv-fitting of delta function, elliptical/circular Gaussian and disc models for Mira A and B per epoch

recipe.goal: Derive spectral indices and brightness temperatures
recipe.method: Spectral index within Band 3 from MFS/uv-fits and between bands from flux densities; Tb for uniform disc

recipe.goal: Compare with radio photosphere and wind models
recipe.method: Compare SED/spectral index and Tb with Reid & Menten model and expected Mira B wind emission
assumptions: Ionized cavity gas temperature T=10^4 K
